analysis_steps.goal: Align MUSE cubes to the ALMA continuum

method.value: Measure reference points in MUSE and ALMA continuum images and shift the ALMA coordinates to match MUSE; for most proplyds the MUSE star position (continuum subcube 674-678 nm) is matched to the ALMA disk center; for 177-341W two background sources seen in both datasets are used

evidence.quote: The alignment was done by measuring relevant references points in the MUSE and ALMA continuum images and shifting the coordinates of the ALMA image to align with MUSE.
we carried out the matching by using two background sources present in both the ALMA and MUSE data

key_parameters.value: Alignment uncertainty taken as half the MUSE spaxel size (0.0125"), or 0.025" spaxel for 168-326, 174-414 and 203-504

evidence.quote: We considered the uncertainty on this alignment to be half the spatial size of the MUSE spaxels (0.0125")

analysis_steps.goal: Overlay MUSE line contours on ALMA images

method.value: MUSE line emission shown as contours at 50%, 70% and 90% of the peak intensity over the ALMA Band 7 images

evidence.quote: which is shown with contours representing 50%, 70% and 90% of the peak intensity of the line emission

analysis_steps.goal: Derive disk inclinations and position angles from ALMA

method.value: Inclinations from deconvolved FWHM major and minor axes listed by Ballering et al. 2023, or from CASA imfit on the ALMA data for 168-326 and 171-340

evidence.quote: We report the inclinations of the disks, calculated from their deconvolved FWHM major and minor axes listed by (cite: ballering2023) and calculated using the CASA task imfit on the ALMA data for proplyds 168-326 and 171-340.

analysis_steps.goal: Measure line-peak offsets from the star with radial cuts

method.value: Emission along a 6" long line centered on the star (disk center for 177-341W) and oriented toward theta1 Ori C, on the MUSE emission-line images; offset of the line peak from the star, positive toward the UV source

evidence.quote: This was performed by calculating the emission along a 6" long line centered at the coordinates of the central star and oriented towards the ionizing source
The positive sign of the values on y-axis marks a peak located in the direction of the UV source, and the negative sign the opposite.

validation.value: Offsets compared with the alignment uncertainty (half spaxel); most are compatible with zero within the uncertainties

evidence.quote: The values are compatible with no displacement within their uncertainties

analysis_steps.goal: Compute relative inclination of each disk with respect to the UV source

method.value: Spherical law of cosines using the ALMA disk position angle and inclination and the star-UV source position angle

evidence.quote: we calculate the relative inclination of the disks using the spherical law of cosines

assumptions.value: Inclination of the UV source emission in the plane of the sky taken as i2 = 90 deg

evidence.quote: the inclination we assume for the emission coming from the UV source in the plane of the sky

claims.hypothesis: The [C I] 8727 line arises from the disk surface/base of the external photoevaporative wind in proplyds
claims.experiment: Aligned MUSE-NFM line maps with ALMA Band 7 continuum for 6 proplyds and with the MUSE stellar continuum for all 12, and compared contours and peak offsets
claims.result: [C I] 8727 contours follow the ALMA disk shape, with peak compatible with the star in all but 177-341W
claims.finding: [C I] 8727 is co-spatial with the disk surface and not the ionization front

evidence.quote: is also co-spatial with the disk surface in a proplyd, as seen in the MUSE and ALMA data comparison
The alignment was done by measuring relevant references points in the MUSE and ALMA continuum images and shifting the coordinates of the ALMA image to align with MUSE.

claims.hypothesis: The two [O I] lines trace different regions in proplyds
claims.experiment: Compared MUSE [O I] 5577 and 6300 contours with the ALMA disk continuum and the stellar continuum
claims.result: [O I] 5577 is co-spatial with the disk; [O I] 6300 comes from both the disk and the ionization front
claims.finding: Confirms earlier results that 5577 is a disk tracer and 6300 also traces the ionization front

evidence.quote: 6300 Å is emitted both on the disk surface and on the ionization front of the proplyds

claims.hypothesis: [C I] 8727 is a tell-tale tracer of external photoevaporation, absent in isolated disks
claims.experiment: Compared detection rates of [C I] 8727 and [O I] in X-Shooter spectra of PENELLOPE (low-mass SFRs) and sigma-Orionis targets with the 12 ONC proplyds
claims.result: One clear plus 7 tentative detections of 74 in PENELLOPE (<<10%), ~40% in sigma-Orionis, 12 of 12 in ONC
claims.finding: Detection rate rises with external UV field, supporting the FUV-pumping excitation models

evidence.quote: strongly suggest that this line is a tell-tale tracer of externally driven photoevaporative winds, which agrees with recent excitation models.

claims.hypothesis: The offset of the line peak toward the UV source depends on the disk inclination relative to the UV source
claims.experiment: Computed relative inclinations with the spherical law of cosines for the six proplyds with ALMA inclinations and compared with peak offsets
claims.result: Only 177-341W (highest relative inclination) has a significant offset
claims.finding: Possible explanation, needing a larger sample

evidence.quote: This hypothesis needs confirmation on a larger sample of targets.

why_this_data.value: ALMA Band 7 traces the thermal dust disk, giving a reference position for the disk against which the MUSE line emission is compared

evidence.quote: The ALMA Band 7 data trace thermal dust emission from the disk
show that the Band 7 data does not trace the ionization front

why_this_method.value: MUSE-NFM astrometry is uncertain, so the cubes must be aligned to ALMA before comparing positions

evidence.quote: As MUSE-NFM is known to have uncertain astrometric accuracy, it is necessary to align the MUSE cubes with the ALMA data

limitations_admitted.value: Disk inclination and position angle are missing for half of the sample (no ALMA data), so the relative-inclination explanation cannot be tested further

evidence.quote: The lack of measurements of the disk inclination and position angle for half of our sample hinders the possibility to further confirm this is due to the relative inclination of the disks and the external UV radiation.

limitations_admitted.value: The relative-inclination hypothesis needs a larger sample

evidence.quote: This hypothesis needs confirmation on a larger sample of targets.

referee_caveats_inferred: ALMA is used only as a positional reference; no ALMA reduction or imaging details are given
Offsets are mostly consistent with zero within half-spaxel uncertainties, so the comparison depends on the alignment assumption that the star sits at the ALMA disk center
Detection rates in X-Shooter spectra rest on unstated S/N criteria and different spectral resolution and sensitivity from MUSE-NFM
Inclination and PA are missing for 6 of 12 proplyds and two values rely on a paper in prep.

data_public_as_stated.value: X-Shooter PENELLOPE spectra are stated to be publicly available; ALMA and MUSE availability not stated beyond the acknowledgement of ALMA project 2015.1.00534.S

evidence.quote: Lastly, we use the publicly available spectra taken with VLT/X-Shooter for the PENELLOPE Large Program (cite: manara2021)

missing_for_reproduction: ALMA calibration and imaging recipe (only a reference to Eisner et al. 2018)
MUSE reduction and line-map construction (deferred to Aru et al. 2024 and Haworth et al. 2023)
Line-detection criteria for the X-Shooter spectra
Inclinations for 168-326 and 171-340 from a paper in prep.
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Tens of GB for the six ALMA Band 7 datasets plus MUSE-NFM cubes (not stated in the paper)
reproducibility.score_reason: The ALMA part is a positional comparison with no processing recipe, the MUSE inputs are deferred to other papers, and the numeric results are few offsets and detection rates.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: MUSE processing and ALMA reduction are deferred to other papers, and the main conclusions are largely qualitative spatial comparisons.
